rv.q: This razor-sharp production has crisp, clear direction.
It's a modern, compelling and extremely relevant production. Highly recommended.
Burns not produced an interpretation of the work that turns one of the so-called 'problem plays' into a terrific piece of contemporary theatre that grips from start to finish.
Emily Burns’ lucid modern-day adaptation paints a bleak picture of a corrupt political system
It's a decent attempt at making sense of a play that often refuses to be wrangled intelligibly for modern audiences. I just wish it didn't labour its point quite so heavily.
The crucial ambiguity inherent in the silence duly preserved, if a little over-egged, this Measure is properly powerful...

Measure for Measure has been described as one of his 'problem plays' but in this very fine edited version, it resonates wonderfully in today's society with the counter position of moral dilemmas, political expediency, human base instincts and the corruption of power.
It's the intensity of the playing that makes this production stand out.

cn.t: Emily Burns' modern RSC production earns acclaim for its timely resonance and streamlined storytelling, with critics praising its laser focus on power and hypocrisy, superb performances, and uncompromising contemporary edge.
